content: 1. The P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter plays a role in drug interactions. Use caution and monitor when co-administering drugs that inhibit P-gp, as they may increase the levels of substrates like naldemedine, potentially leading to adverse effects. 2. Both nilotinib and quinine can prolong the QTc interval. Exercise caution and monitor patients closely when these drugs are used together. 3. Quinine increases the levels of nintedanib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy may need to be modified, and close monitoring is required. If adverse effects of nintedanib occur, consider dose reduction, therapy interruption, or discontinuation. 4. Nortriptyline and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 5. Octreotide and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 6. Ofloxacin and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 7. Olanzapine and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 8. Quinine increases the levels or effects of oliceridine by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy may need to be modified, and close monitoring is required. If co-administration is necessary, reduce oliceridine dosing frequency and monitor for respiratory depression and sedation. Adjust subsequent doses accordingly. If the inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing the oliceridine dosage until stable drug effects are achieved. Monitor for signs of opioid withdrawal. 9. Quinine and olodaterol (inhaled) both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Drugs that prolong the QTc interval may potentiate the cardiovascular effects of beta-2 agonists, increasing the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. 10. Omaveloxolone decreases the levels or effects of quinine by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Omaveloxolone may reduce systemic exposure of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. Check prescribing information for dosage modification if needed. 11. Oritavancin decreases the levels or effects of quinine by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Oritavancin is a weak CYP3A4 inducer; exercise caution when co-administering with CYP3A4 substrates that have a narrow therapeutic index. 12. Osilodrostat and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 13. Oxaliplatin increases the levels or effects of quinine through other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Monitor for ECG changes if therapy is initiated in patients taking drugs known to prolong the QT interval. 14. Ozanimod and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy may need to be modified, and close monitoring is required. Due to potential additive effects on heart rate, treatment with ozanimod should generally not be initiated in patients concurrently treated with QT-prolonging drugs with known arrhythmogenic properties. 15. Quinine increases the levels or effects of paclitaxel by other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Paclitaxel levels and toxicity may increase when co-administered with CYP2C8 inhibitors. 16. Quinine increases the levels or effects of paclitaxel protein-bound by other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Paclitaxel levels and toxicity may increase when co-administered with CYP2C8 inhibitors. 17. Palbociclib increases the levels or effects of quinine by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy may need to be modified, and close monitoring is required. The dose of sensitive CYP3A substrates with a narrow therapeutic index may need to be reduced if co-administered with palbociclib. 18. Paliperidone and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 19. Quinine and pasireotide both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy may need to be modified, and close monitoring is required. 20. Pazopanib and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 21. Pentamidine and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 22. Perphenazine and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 23. Phenytoin decreases the levels or effects of quinine by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. When prescribing phenytoin and quinine together, be aware of decreased quinine plasma concentrations and potential lack of efficacy. 24. Pirtobrutinib increases the levels or effects of quinine by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Pirtobrutinib (a CYP3A4 inhibitor) may increase plasma concentrations of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates, increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 25. Pitolisant decreases the levels or effects of quinine by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Pitolisant is a borderline/weak inducer of CYP3A4. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for reduced effectiveness if co-administered. 26. Posaconazole and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 27. Procainamide increases the levels or effects of quinine by basic (cationic) drug competition for renal tubular clearance. Procainamide and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 28. Propafenone and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 29. Protriptyline and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 30. Quetiapine and quinine increase each other's toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Avoid use with drugs that prolong QT and in patients with risk factors for prolonged QT interval. Postmarketing cases show QT prolongation with overdose in patients with concomitant illness or drugs known to cause electrolyte imbalance or prolong QT. 31. Quinidine increases the levels or effects of quinine by basic (cationic) drug competition for renal tubular clearance. Quinidine and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 32. Quizartinib and quinine increase each other's effects by prolonging the QTc interval. Therapy may need to be modified, and close monitoring is required. Monitor patients more frequently with ECG if co-administered with QT-prolonging drugs. 33. Ranolazine and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 34. Ribociclib increases the levels or effects of quinine by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy may need to be modified, and close monitoring is required. Exercise caution if ribociclib is co-administered with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates that have a narrow therapeutic index. Dose reduction for sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may be needed. 35. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of quinine by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 36. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of quinine by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 37. Quinine increases the levels of rifaximin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 38. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of quinine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Rilpivirine should be used cautiously when co-administered with a drug with a known risk of Torsade de Pointes. 39. Risperidone and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 40. Ritlecitinib increases the levels or effects of quinine by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy may need to be modified, and close monitoring is required. Ritlecitinib inhibits CYP3A4 substrates; co-administration increases AUC and peak plasma concentration of sensitive substrates, which may increase the risk of adverse reactions. Additional monitoring and dosage adjustment may be needed in accordance with product labeling of CYP3A substrates. 41. Romidepsin and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 42. Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of quinine by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy may need to be modified, and close monitoring is required. Adjust the dosage of CYP3A4 substrates if clinically indicated. 43. Saredcycline increases the levels or effects of quinine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Monitor for toxicities of P-gp substrates that may require dosage reduction when co-administered with P-gp inhibitors. 44. Sarilumab may alter the formation of CYP450 enzymes due to increased cytokine levels such as IL-6. Elevated IL-6 concentrations may down-regulate CYP activity, increasing drug levels compared to subjects without RA. IL-6 blockade by IL-6 antagonists (e.g., sarilumab) might reverse this inhibitory effect and restore CYP activity, leading to decreased drug concentrations. Use caution when initiating or discontinuing sarilumab if co-administered with CYP450 substrates, especially those with a narrow therapeutic index. 45. Schisandra increases the levels or effects of quinine by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 46. Secukinumab may normalize the formation of CYP450 enzymes during chronic inflammation by altering cytokine levels. Upon initiation or discontinuation of secukinumab in patients receiving concomitant CYP450 substrates, particularly those with a narrow therapeutic index, consider monitoring for therapeutic effect. 47. Quinine increases the levels or effects of selexipag by decreasing metabolism. Therapy may need to be modified, and close monitoring is required. Reduce the selexipag dose to once daily if co-administered with moderate CYP2C8 inhibitors. 48. Selpercatinib increases the toxicity of quinine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 49. Sertraline and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 50. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride increases the toxicity of quinine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Consider pre-dose and post-colonoscopy ECGs in patients at increased risk of serious cardiac arrhythmias. 51. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate increases the toxicity of quinine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Consider pre-dose and post-colonoscopy ECGs in patients at increased risk of serious cardiac arrhythmias. 52. Solifenacin and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 53. Somapacitan decreases the levels or effects of quinine by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Limited published data indicate that growth hormone treatment increases cytochrome P450 (CYP450)-mediated antipyrine clearance. Exercise caution with sensitive CYP substrates. 54. Somatrogon decreases the levels or effects of quinine by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Limited published data indicate that growth hormone treatment increases cytochrome P450 (CYP450)-mediated antipyrine clearance. Exercise caution with sensitive CYP substrates. 55. Somatropin decreases the levels or effects of quinine by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Limited published data indicate that growth hormone treatment increases cytochrome P450 (CYP450)-mediated antipyrine clearance. Exercise caution with sensitive CYP substrates. 56. Sorafenib and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 57. Sotalol and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 58. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of quinine by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 59. Stiripentol affects hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and may increase or decrease the effects of quinine. Therapy may need to be modified, and close monitoring is required. Stiripentol is both a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer. Monitor CYP3A4 substrates co-administered with stiripentol for increased or decreased effects. 60. Stiripentol increases the levels or effects of quinine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy may need to be modified, and close monitoring is required. Consider reducing the dose of P-glycoprotein (P-gp) substrates if adverse reactions are experienced when administered concomitantly with stiripentol. 61. Sunitinib and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 62. Tacrolimus and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 63. Quinine increases the levels or effects of talazoparib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Talazoparib is a P-glycoprotein (P-gp) substrate; co-administration with P-gp inhibitors may increase talazoparib systemic exposure. 64. Talquetamab increases the levels or effects of quinine by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Talquetamab causes cytokine release syndrome (CRS), which may suppress CYP enzyme activity, resulting in increased exposure of CYP substrates. This is more likely to occur from initiation of talquetamab step-up dosing up to 14 days after the first treatment dose and during and after CRS. 65. Quinine increases the levels of tamsulosin by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 66. Tazemetostat decreases the levels or effects of quinine by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Quinine increases the levels or effects of tazemetostat by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 67. Teclistamab increases the levels or effects of quinine by altering metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Teclistamab causes cytokine release that may suppress CYP450 enzyme activity, resulting in increased exposure of CYP substrates. Monitor for increased concentrations or toxicities of sensitive CYP substrates. Adjust the dose of CYP substrate drugs as needed. 68. Tecovirimat decreases the levels or effects of quinine by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Tecovirimat is a weak CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness if co-administered. 69. Telavancin and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 70. Telotristat ethyl decreases the levels or effects of quinine by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy may need to be modified, and close monitoring is required. Telotristat ethyl induces CYP3A4 and may reduce systemic exposure of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. Monitor for suboptimal efficacy and consider increasing the dose of the CYP3A4 substrate. 71. Tetracaine and quinine may interact through other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Monitor for signs of methemoglobinemia when methemoglobin-inducing drugs are co-administered. 72. Thiothixene and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 73. Quinine increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 74. Tobramycin (inhaled) and quinine both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Therapy may need to be modified, and close monitoring is required. Avoid concurrent or sequential use to decrease the risk of ototoxicity. 75. Toremifene and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 76. Triclabendazole and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 77. Trimipramine and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 78. Trofinetide increases the levels or effects of quinine by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients closely. Monitor CYP3A4 substrates for which a small increase in plasma concentration may lead to serious toxicities if co-administered with trofinetide (a weak CYP3A4 inhibitor). 79. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of quinine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor patients closely.
